attachments.origin_landmark: costal cartilages 7-12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lateral inguinal ligament
attachments.insertion_landmark: linea alba (via aponeurosis) and pubic crest; lowest fibers contribute to the conjoint tendon

actions: compresses abdominal contents / raises intra-abdominal pressure
feedforward stabilization of the lumbar spine preceding limb movement

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Deepest of the three flat abdominal layers; fibers run purely horizontally (transversely), distinct from both overlying oblique layers -- functionally the primary intrinsic spinal stabilizer of the group, with well-documented feedforward (anticipatory) activation before limb movement.
functional_compartments.source: Hodges PW, Richardson CA (1996) Spine 21(22):2640-2650 -- transversus abdominis's role in lumbar spine stabilization (feedforward activation preceding limb movement)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Hodges PW, Richardson CA (1996) Spine 21(22):2640-2650 -- transversus abdominis's role in lumbar spine stabilization (feedforward activation preceding limb movement)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Same window again -- transverse, mid-axillary line, between costal margin and iliac crest -- reading the deepest of the three layers.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deepest of the three flat lateral wall muscles, directly superficial to the transversalis fascia and peritoneum.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Fibers run transversely (horizontally); the transversus abdominis plane lies immediately superficial to it, between it and internal oblique.
structures_at_risk: peritoneum and bowel immediately deep to the muscle -- the floor beyond which a needle should not pass
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: The muscle most affected by preoperative lateral-wall botulinum toxin before complex ventral hernia repair: up to ~330% elongation and a volume INCREASE reported on volumetric CT, unlike the obliques, which elongate but lose volume -- consistent with transversus abdominis being the muscle component-separation surgery itself targets for release.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Quevedo-Cruz D et al., Hernia 30:75 (2026), doi:10.1007/s10029-025-03558-7 -- ultrasound-guided botulinum toxin prehabilitation technique for complex ventral hernia (PubMed); Zamkowski M et al., Pol Przegl Chir 97(6):1 (2025), doi:10.5604/01.3001.0055.3078 -- volumetric muscle elongation by layer after lateral wall injection (PubMed)
